Listening script (the audio is coming soon; until then, read it aloud with a volunteer at a normal, friendly speed):
Narrator: Lesson nine. Listening. Lucia has a job interview at a hotel. Mr. Hall is the manager. Listen.
Mr. Hall: Hi, Lucia. Thank you for coming in. Please sit down. So, tell me about yourself.
Lucia: Well, I have three years of experience in maintenance. I worked at a big apartment building.
Mr. Hall: That's great. What are you good at?
Lucia: I'm good at fixing things, and I'm good at solving problems.
Mr. Hall: Are you reliable?
Lucia: Yes. I was never late at my last job, and I always finish my work.
Mr. Hall: Good. Do you enjoy working on a team?
Lucia: Yes, I enjoy helping people. I like teamwork.
Mr. Hall: Are you interested in training? We have a class for new workers.
Lucia: Yes! I'm very interested in learning about the machines here.
Mr. Hall: Which shift can you work?
Lucia: I can work the day shift. And I don't mind working weekends.
Mr. Hall: Great. I'd like you to meet our team. Can you come back on Thursday for a second interview?
Lucia: Yes, of course. Thank you!
Narrator: That's the end of the listening.
slides.title: Before You Listen

Box 4 (2 min): read the spelling rows: fix → fixing, organize → organizing (no e), shop → shopping (double letter). Each click shows one row.

slides.notes:
Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: Interview Rotation · 12 min. Two circles: the inner circle are managers; the outer circle are applicants.
Before (2 min): each manager chooses a job card (1–4: warehouse, hotel, kitchen, childcare) and the Manager Questions. Each applicant fills in the "My answers" box on their page (strengths, experience, shifts). Invented details are fine.
Model with one learner (1 min): you are the manager at the hotel (card 2). "Tell me about yourself." → (answer) → "What are you good at?" → (answer) → follow-up: "Can you give me an example?"
Rotation (6 min): each interview is about 2 minutes: the manager asks 3 questions from the card and one follow-up, then writes one strength in the notes table. Then say "Move!" The outer circle moves one person to the right. 3 rotations. Each click shows the next step.
Switch (3 min): managers and applicants change places for one or two more rotations. Finish: ask 2 managers: "Who gets a second interview? Why?" (Ana, because she's good at organizing.) If behind: 2 rotations, no role switch.
Invented job histories are fine (important): invite, don't require, real job details. Learners can talk about home, family, or volunteer work, or invent a job history. Never ask about immigration or work status, papers, or pay.

runs.t: I can say what I'm good at.
I can say what I'm interested in.
I can talk about my experience.
I can answer Tell me about yourself.
A. Listen to the teacher. Circle a or b.
a. He can fix cars.   b. He wants to learn about cars.
a. She works with children now.   b. She wants to work with children.
a. Night work is OK for him.   b. Night work is a problem for him.
a. He doesn't like cooking.   b. He likes cooking for his family.

slides.notes:
Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min. Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read each sentence slowly, 2 times. Learners circle a or b. Then click to show the answer (one click per item, 1 to 4).
Say: 1 "He's good at fixing cars." (a) • 2 "She's interested in working with children." (b) • 3 "He doesn't mind working at night." (a) • 4 "He enjoys cooking for his family." (b)
Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only. B answers: 1 at, 2 in, 3 working, 4 helping. C: answers will vary (for example I'm good at organizing. I organize the shelves at my job. / I'm interested in learning about computers.).
Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
Scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing the phrases (A) and with at / in + -ing (B, C).
Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 11). If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 11 at 6:00, while learners arrive.
